_about: Reviewed expectations for the three memory_log_a2981a7_*.md fixtures: production-shaped memory logs WRITTEN BY THE FORK AT a2981a7 (what alpha-pulse's server holds today). They were produced by driving a2981a7's own TradingMemoryLog.store_decision, TradingAgentsGraph._resolve_pending_entries and scrub_account_numbers with stubbed prices and a stubbed reflection: per-ticker KR and US logs (the layout alpha-pulse uses) and the legacy shared file; a legacy 6-field tag (settled before #1251 stored a resolution date), resolved tags with resolved:YYYY-MM-DD, pending tags, Korean prose, [redacted] account figures, a free-text decision, and a Revision line that quotes another rating. 'past_context' is get_past_context(ticker) ('live', as_of=None: what a same-day nightly run injects into the Portfolio Manager) and get_past_context(ticker, as_of='2026-09-10') (a historical run), stored as lines. Review: every block was checked by hand against the log text (most recent first, resolved:-field dropped from the rendered tag, pending entries excluded, as_of keeps only entries resolved on/before the cutoff so the legacy tag drops out, cross-ticker lessons as '[date | ticker | rating | raw]' + reflection); the a2981a7 reader, upstream v0.5.1 (35543d0 tradingagents/decision_log.py) and upstream 9968bd8 (tradingagents/memory/log.py) produce this document byte for byte. Never regenerate it from the code under test: these logs already exist in production, and the point is that a merged reader must still read them the same way.
